messages:
ajay: Ran nsys on the 8k-token stress run against staging-dedicated (p99 spike). Timeline shows huge compile/warmup blocks at the start of each worker. Attaching snippets below.

ajay: nsys summary (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)  Name
1200      triton_kernel_compile (nvrtc / JIT)
300       load_cubin_to_device
20        cudaLaunchKernel main_attn
8         kernel exec (matmul_fused)

Total warmup (first request): ~1.6s per model shard
Subsequent requests (after cache hit): ~5-10ms per token
```

lenora: Hmm. Are these NVRTC compilations or Triton caching misses? any `cubin` cache hits/misses in the trace? :eyes:

ajay: It's NVRTC + Triton-style compile steps. Perfetto timeline shows repeated nvrtcCompileProgram events on worker startup and then repeated cubin uploads. Looks like kernel cache is cold for a lot of generated variants (different seq_len / head configs). Example timeline snippet: `nvrtcCompileProgram -> cuModuleLoadData -> cuFuncGetAttribute -> cudaLaunchKernel` repeated ~12 times in first 2s.

maria: Do we persist the kernel cache between processes? I thought we wrote compiled cubins to disk under /var/lib/rwinfer/kernel_cache. If that's not being mounted on dedicated, we'll recompile on every container start.

ajay: On dedicated pool the worker starts per-GPU container and kernel_cache is ephemeral; no shared volume. Also note batching heuristic: very small initial batches (1-2) across many workers triggering different compile parameters (prefix_len differences). That multiplies JIT variants.

kai: I can reproduce locally. Running: `python -m rwinfer.bench --model redwood-7b --seq 8192 --profile nsys --workers 4` shows the same pattern. nvprof shows ~1.1-1.3s spent in NVRTC for first 8 kernels. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.app/trace/FAKE-EXAMPLE (screenshot attached in thread).

kai: Observed kernel cache miss rate ~78% on first minute, drops to ~5% after priming. So warmup cost dominates tail latency for short-lived workers.

maria: Two mitigations off top: 1) persist kernel cache across worker restarts (shared mount or S3-backed cache), 2) batch priming step at worker startup to precompile the high-frequency kernels for common seq lengths.

ajay: Agreed. Also the compilation time is sensitive to compile flags we pass to Triton (we enable a lot of fusions which increases compile time). For tradeoff experiments we could add a fast-fallback kernel selection: prefer precompiled generic kernels for first N requests and switch to optimized fused ones after cache.

perf-bot: Perf alert: perf/regression-checker detected +18% p99 for `dedicated-hyperslice` after merge `a3b9f2`. Relevant CI job: https://ci/reds/perf/6721

lenora: Oof. That lines up with the PR that introduced extra Triton fusions last week. @kai can you validate whether disabling the new fusion fixes the warmup?

kai: Yup. Quick toggle: in runtime conf set `TRITON_ENABLE_FUSION=false` and restart worker -> warmup drops from ~1.6s to ~0.4s, but per-token steady-state slower by ~6-8%. So it's a classic warmup vs steady-state tradeoff.

ajay: Notes from nsys timeline analysis: hotspots are NVRTC (compile) and cuModuleLoadData (cubin load). Kernel-launch latency negligible once compiled. Also KV-cache behavior: initial KV writes cause extra small kernels (kv_memcpy) that themselves trigger new kernel variants for small batch sizes. So two axes: kernel compilation and KV growth interaction.

maria: Suggestion: change batching heuristic to coalesce first 2-3 requests within 50ms window into a priming batch to reduce variant churn. Also add a background priming job on worker startup that runs a short sequence to generate main kv shapes and compile top ~10 kernels.

kai: I'll prototype the priming batch heuristic. Quick experiment plan:
```
Experiment A: Persist kernel cache (shared dir) + current fusion flags
Experiment B: Disable fusion for first 30s, enable later (fast-fallback)
Experiment C: Startup priming workload (2s) + coalesce small batches
```

ajay: I'll own kernel cache persistence + CI nsys job (adds reproducible trace generation). Maria can you open infra ticket for mounting shared kernel cache on dedicated pool?

maria: Creating infra ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-7318 (notes: mount /var/lib/rwinfer/kernel_cache on all dedicated GPUs; provide retention policy).

lenora: I'll file product/telemetry tasks: expose a metric `kernel_cache_hit_rate` and `compile_time_ms` in Console so we can watch priming. Also add eval that fails if first-request p99 > 1s.

ajay: Action items: 1) PR for kernel cache persistence (ajay) 2) CI nsys perf job + baseline trace (ajay) 3) batching priming heuristic (kai) 4) infra mount (maria) 5) telemetry + alert (lenora). I can draft the PR for (1) and a reproducible script: `tools/profile/warmup_repro.sh`.

kai: Quick note on implementation: kernel_cache must be sharded by model+arch+cc to avoid cross-model collisions. Also store metadata JSON alongside cubin with compile flags.

ajay: Good call. We'll key by `model:sha256(config+weights):cuda_arch:triton_flags`.

maria: One more: watch out for disk pressure if we persist all variants. Add LRU eviction and a max-size (default 10GB).

lenora: ACK. I'll put the telemetry and eviction policy into the RFC.

ajay: I'll push an initial PR today with tests that run `nsys` in CI in a lightweight mode and assert compile time < 700ms on baseline. Assigning reviewers: @lenora, @maria.

kai: I'll start prototyping the priming heuristic branch and post a small perf run later today. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks team. This explains most of the p99 uptick. Keep thread updated with any new traces.

perf-bot: CI Trace Uploaded: https://ci/trace/abc123-qdrep (automated).
